findings.issue: Move-table construction (dedup key method|move|level, method rank order, level-then-name default sort, version-group fallback selection) is completely untested — it's the most intricate logic in the app.
findings.suggestion: Extract the move-table builder and version-group selection into pure functions taking API-shaped input and test them against small fixtures (fixture data can be plain objects; no HTTP needed).

findings.issue: URL-driven filtering (type/generation/q matching), page clamping, 48-per-page slicing and reset-to-page-1 are untested; an off-by-one or clamp regression would pass.
findings.suggestion: Extract the matches/page/results computation as pure functions of (vm, params) and unit-test edge cases: empty query params, page beyond pageCount, zero matches, name matching case-insensitivity against humanized names.

findings.issue: toCards' alternate-form exclusion (id < 10000), dedup and dex ordering are untested; a wrong comparison silently leaks Mega forms or drops species.
findings.suggestion: Test toCards with refs including ID 10000+ and duplicate species entries, asserting exclusion, dedup and ascending order.

findings.issue: Sort comparator (missing values last in BOTH directions, numeric vs localeCompare, tie-break by name) and aria-sort flipping are untested; asc/desc parity bugs are easy to introduce.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator and sortBy state transition into pure functions and test nulls-last in both directions plus the ascending→descending toggle.

findings.issue: latestFlavorText (last English entry) and collapse (whitespace/\f runs) are untested — spec-pinned behaviour with classic index/regex bugs.
findings.suggestion: Add cases: only non-English entries, entries with \f and \n, $effect_chance substitution in shortEffect.

findings.issue: toUrl marker parsing, idFromUrl regex and cache eviction are untested; a URL-parsing regression breaks every page.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test toUrl with the three accepted shapes (bare path, /api/v2/... path, absolute URL) and idFromUrl with and without trailing slash.

findings.issue: PageData's TransferState consume-once hydration and the /_data fetch's 404→null / non-ok→throw mapping are untested; hydration double-fetches or error-swallowing would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Test load() with a fake loader and TransferState: present key returns cached value and removes it; second call hits the loader; fetch 404 resolves null.

findings.issue: loadPageData path routing (malformed %-escapes → null, extra segments → null, missing name → null) is untested and defines which URLs 404.
findings.suggestion: Test the router table directly: '/pokemon/pikachu?game=x', '/home/x', '%zz' — expect null.

summary: The agent wrote exactly three unit tests for the pure formatting helpers; they're behavioural, lean and each pins a real spec rule (including the falsy-zero em-dash trap), but they cover the least risky code in the app. The high-risk logic — the 400-line server-side view-model builder, URL-state filtering/pagination, and the sortable move tables — is entirely untested, so a refactor of the data layer after acceptance testing ends would be unguarded. Overall the test suite is a token effort: correct in style, negligible in coverage.
valuableTests: format — shows missing values as an em dash (asserts orDash(0) === '0') — would catch a rewrite to `value || '—'` that blanks out legitimate zero values
format — humanizes API names (mr-mime → Mr Mime, thunder-punch → Thunder Punch) — pins the spec's display-name rule used on every list page
format — formats dex numbers (25 → #0025, 1026 → #1026) — pins the zero-padding and non-padding-above-9999 rules
